review_cost.rationale: Approve after one small round: two genuine fixes (promise-cache retry semantics, unreachable error state) and a handful of nits; no architectural rework needed.

findings.issue: Rejected promises are cached permanently: a single transient API error (e.g. on the species list) leaves that resource broken for the whole session with no retry path.
findings.suggestion: Only cache successful resolutions (cache the promise but delete the entry on rejection), or add a retry/error-invalidation policy.

findings.issue: Effect copies resource.value() into a separate `view` signal — the effect-to-signal propagation the Angular effects docs explicitly warn against — and it makes the `@else if (data.error())` branch (line 107) unreachable once any data has loaded, so failed reloads silently show stale results.
findings.suggestion: Drive the template from the resource plus an `isLoading()` overlay for stale-while-loading, or at minimum reset `view` to null when `data.error()` is set, and comment the intent either way.

findings.issue: Hash-scroll to #moves uses an untracked setTimeout inside an effect: it races with rendering, is never cleaned up on destroy, and re-fires on every game change.
findings.suggestion: Use afterRenderEffect (the documented tool for post-render DOM work) with onCleanup, or Router's withInMemoryScrolling({ anchorScrolling: 'enabled' }).

findings.issue: Selecting a new game navigates without preserveFragment, dropping the #moves anchor and resetting the viewport.
findings.suggestion: Pass { preserveFragment: true } (or re-append the fragment) in the navigate extras.

findings.issue: The 'speciesById map + exclude alternate forms + sort by id' block is duplicated nearly verbatim in type-page.ts:105-117 and ability-page.ts:71-84.
findings.suggestion: Extract a `speciesCards(refs: NamedRef[])` helper on PokedexData so the alternate-form rule lives in one place.

findings.issue: The em-dash 'missing value' formatter exists three times (also move-page.ts:96-97 and the unused helpers.ts displayValue:65-67).
findings.suggestion: Delete the copies and import displayValue from core/helpers in both components.

findings.issue: No loader passes or checks abortSignal (also pokemon-page.ts:237); the resource docs mandate forwarding it, and rapid filter typing runs concurrent loaders.
findings.suggestion: Accept the abortSignal from the loader context and check it after each await (or pass it through to the underlying HTTP layer).

findings.issue: Search updates the URL and re-runs the loader on every keystroke with no debounce (the spec allows up to 300 ms).
findings.suggestion: Debounce the search input ~200-300 ms before navigating; cheap today only because of the promise cache.

findings.issue: No unit tests at all (0 test files, no test runner in devDependencies) while an `ng test` script exists.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest per the framework's testing guidance, at least for helpers.ts (humanize, latestEnglishFlavor, dexNumber) and MoveTable sorting.

findings.issue: Duplicate import statements from @angular/core (Service on its own line), and zero explanatory comments anywhere in the TS sources despite non-obvious reactive patterns.
findings.suggestion: Merge imports (prettier organize-imports) and add short 'why' comments on the view-signal mirror and the moveTables/base chaining.

summary: A genuinely modern, well-typed Angular 22 codebase that follows current guidance (resource, @Service, signal inputs, withComponentInputBinding, lazy standalone routes) with clean PokeApi/PokedexData/shared-component boundaries. The main review asks are small but real: permanently cached rejected promises, the home page's effect-mirrored `view` signal that hides error states, and a setTimeout hash-scroll hack instead of afterRenderEffect. I'd merge after one short round of fixes plus a few copy-paste consolidations.
